content: We need a retrosynthesis route with max 1 step (i.e., direct synthesis from commercially available precursors). The target is a stilbene derivative: (E)-1,2-bis(4-methoxyphenyl)ethene? Actually SMILES: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2. That's trans-1,2-bis(4-methoxyphenyl)ethene (p-methoxystyrene dimer). Could be synthesized via Heck coupling of 4-methoxyiodobenzene with 4-methoxyphenylacetylene? No, need double bond between two aryl groups. Classic route: Wittig reaction between 4-methoxybenzaldehyde and a phosphonium ylide derived from 4-methoxybenzyl bromide? Actually stilbene can be made via Wittig: 4-methoxybenzaldehyde + (4-methoxyphenyl)triphenylphosphonium bromide (or ylide). That is one step (Wittig) from commercially available 4-methoxybenzaldehyde and (4-methoxyphenyl)triphenylphosphonium bromide (maybe not commercially). Another route: McMurry coupling of two equivalents of 4-methoxybenzaldehyde using TiCl4/Zn. That's a single step coupling of aldehydes. Both aldehydes are commercially available. So retrosynthesis: target -> two 4-methoxybenzaldehyde via McMurry coupling (C-C double bond formation). Template likely "aldehydes -> alkene" (McMurry).
